method: leave-individual-out allele-frequency nearest-centroid on chr22 shared SNPs
caveats: This is an allele-frequency nearest-centroid stand-in for the RFMix classification decision, not RFMix itself, and single-chromosome (chr22).
The AJ reference group has only 8 AADR individuals; per-pop accuracy for AJ is a bounded sanity check, NOT a validation of real Ashkenazi ancestry.

OPTIMISM WARNING for AJ: the 8 AJ individuals are array genotypes IMPUTED from the 1000G reference, so their genotypes at analysis sites share an imputation basis and can cluster artificially tightly. A high AJ leave-one-out score here is therefore likely optimistic and must NOT be read as evidence the model distinguishes real AJ ancestry. Genuine validation needs non-imputed, held-out AJ WGS (e.g. the access-controlled Ashkenazi Genome Consortium) and more than one chromosome.
Few shared sites: the AADR Human Origins array overlaps the query markers at only ~2k chr22 positions and the benchmark subset uses even fewer; accuracy on so few sites is high-variance.
Fine 1000G sub-populations within a super-population are known to be hard to separate on one chromosome; low per-pop accuracy for close sub-pops is expected and is reported honestly, not hidden.
Relatives: 1000G Phase 3 is a largely-unrelated panel; no additional related individuals were included in the held-out set.
